1.why: Every MFA endpoint derives identity solely from the HttpOnly session cookie via authorized(), and mutates only auth.user, so no client-supplied user id can be used to reach another account's settings.

2.why: The identity code is stored on the individual session object (session.identityCode) and TOTP/backup codes are per-user, so a code accepted for one session/user cannot validate another.

3.why: /api/mfa/activate only sets mfa.enabled and regenerates backup codes; it never iterates the sessions map to revoke other existing sessions, so previously established sessions remain valid.

4.why: The TOTP secret is stored as AES-GCM ciphertext (encrypt/decrypt with a server-side key) and backup codes are stored only as salted SHA-256 digests with a 'used' flag.

5.why: Secrets, session ids, CSRF tokens, identity codes and recovery codes all come from crypto.getRandomValues / crypto.subtle.generateKey.

6.why: The session cookie is HttpOnly/Secure/SameSite=Strict and no localStorage/sessionStorage is used; CSRF token and provisioning secret live only in transient JS variables/DOM, which is a lesser exposure.

7.why: Server-side regex validators (validEmail, validPhone, validOTP, validRecovery, manualSecret pattern) gate every endpoint, JSON body parsing is guarded, and there is no SQL/in-memory Map lookup injection surface.

8.why: All dynamic values inserted into the page pass through the esc() HTML-entity encoder, and API responses are served as application/json with nosniff.

9.why: The only redirect is a hardcoded 308 to https://localhost:3000/ on the HTTP port; no request-controlled redirect parameter exists anywhere.

10.why: secureHeaders sets HSTS, X-Content-Type-Options, X-Frame-Options: DENY, Referrer-Policy and a CSP with frame-ancestors 'none', plus a nonce-based script/style CSP for the HTML page.

11.why: cookie() and clearedCookie() both emit HttpOnly; Secure; SameSite=Strict with Path=/ and Max-Age.

12.why: Errors are generic with no stack traces, but the API returns testIdentityCode/secret/testOtp in responses and the client console.logs the identity code, current OTP and the full list of backup recovery codes into the console and a visible log panel.

13.why: The identity code has a 5-minute expiry plus an identityUsed flag, TOTP is bound to a 30-second counter with verifiedCounter replay prevention, and backup codes are marked used after a single successful match.

14.why: Identity, TOTP and recovery verification each track failure counts with a 5-attempt threshold and 5-minute lockout, though the counters are per-session and /api/signin itself has no rate limit.

15.why: The session id is regenerated on sign-in and the old session is deleted and replaced after identity verification, with 15-minute idle and 8-hour absolute timeouts and deletion plus cookie clearing on logout.
